sql_publication_counts.scope:
Measure current-library SQL checkpoint counts using disposable synthetic data.

Counts include connection open/close and background service. They are neither
exact fsync counts nor a throughput qualification. No reference library runs.

regressions: CHECK-only coverage repairs still reject invalid postimages, and all original 2–12 MiB statement cases pass at the unchanged 256 MiB working-memory quota.
SQL defaults, updates and deletion publish two text indexes and primary data in one checkpoint for autocommit and session COMMIT, with query visibility.
Normalization retains one exact packed row authority rather than mapping twice.
An exact post-admission footprint refusal waits outside owner/path admission while another connection returns actual replay credits, without raising quotas.
A proven precommit capacity timeout preserves staged COMMIT state and retry applies its increment exactly once.
Canceled capacity sleep returns without another mutation admission.
Drop/recreate and physical/logical generation replacement cannot silently retarget a capacity retry.
SQL asynchronous replay retains bounded runtime reuse; stable allocator proofs are captured once across handoffs.
outcome_contract: Only confirmed precommit capacity refusals retry already-owned postimages. Applied or uncertain outcomes never retry. Generic errors retain abort semantics.
